subject: general
question: What is the advantage of using a differential amplifier in a voltage amplifier circuit?

options.text: It increases the common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) of the amplifier.
It increases the noise sensitivity of the amplifier.
It increases the gain of the amplifier.
It decreases the power consumption of the amplifier.

solution:
__**Explanation:**__

The **main advantage of using a differential amplifier** in a voltage amplifier circuit is its ability to **reject common-mode signals** (such as noise) while amplifying the difference between input signals.

 
• 
 
A differential amplifier provides a **high Common-Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR)**.

 
 
• 
 
This means unwanted noise or interference that appears equally on both inputs is greatly reduced.

 
 
• 
 
As a result, the amplifier gives a **cleaner and more accurate output**.
